title: Greenlight Systems — Strategy & Pipeline Mapping
summary: Introductory GTM alignment between Redwood and Greenlight to map joint accounts, define co-sell motions, agree on success criteria for three pilot opportunities, and calendarize technical validation and exec briefing. Key friction: lead routing, proof-of-value benchmarks, and co-term contracting.
action_items: Alex Chen: Share partner co-sell one-pager and pricing bands; due 2026-02-26
Priya Nair: Prepare test plan and benchmark template for pilot (latency/cost); due 2026-03-03
Diego Morales: Send Greenlight's security questionnaire; due 2026-02-27
Maya Singh: Confirm prioritized list of 8 accounts and owner contact details; due 2026-02-28
next_steps: Set up technical deep dive w/ Greenlight engineering (schedule week of Mar 8)
Exchange redacted SOW template and partner MSA sketch
Run a small 2-week pilot on Redwood Dedicated for Account A to validate latency SLA
Plan an executive alignment (AE+VP Sales) after pilot completion
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-02-24 16:00 UTC | Duration 62m | Attendees listed above

[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. Alex from Redwood here, I think we've got about an hour to walk through GTM alignment and three initial targets. We'll keep it pretty practical, short win focus.
[00:18] Maya Singh: Thanks Alex, appreciate it. I'm Maya, I run partnerships at Greenlight — we've been chatting with Samir and Alex over email. Main objective today is to see how we team up on pipeline and what support we'll get for pilots.
[00:35] Samir Patel: Hi all — Samir from Redwood partner ops. Quick note: we're aiming to make lead routing simple, and we have a standard co-sell comp model but flexible.
[00:50] Jon Park: Jon here, I look after Cloud Ops. From our side we need to understand private deployment cadence — we deal with some regulated telco customers, so VPC/on-prem options matter.
[01:10] Priya Nair: Totally — we can run on Hosted and Dedicated today, and for Private we have a path but it takes longer. Also want to flag some perf artifacts we'll share.
[01:25] Elena Ramos: Elena from sales — I want clarity on reps' motions: who owns the primary relationship, and how do credits/commissions look when we co-sell?
[01:39] Alex Chen: Good Q. Typical model: Greenlight owns the account relationship, Redwood supports with technical sell and a joint demo. We propose a 60/40 revenue split for sourced accounts or a flat referral credit for influenced deals — flexible. We'll follow up with concrete bands.
[01:58] Maya Singh: That aligns with what we did previously on another engagement, but we need firm SLAs for pilot measurement. What KPIs should we track?
[02:12] Priya Nair: For pilots we recommend: p50/p95 latency, token cost per 1k requests, throughput per GPU, and correctness/regression on a small eval set. We'll send a benchmark template.
[02:30] Diego Morales: Can you share the benchmark artifacts? We prefer something reproducible, reproducible scripts — not just screenshots.
[02:42] Priya Nair: Yes, Diego we'll share the test harness GitHub link and a CSV template. Note, our internal names sometimes show up wrong in transcriptions — 'Redwood Optimize' is actually Redwood Optimize (sorry, babble), but the product that suggests batching and quantization is Redwood Optimize.
[03:05] Jon Park: Quick safety question: key management. For private deployments, our security team needs KMS/HSM integration and audit logs. Is that supported?
[03:20] Alex Chen: Yes, KMS integration is supported in Private via our KMS connectors; for Hosted we offer customer-managed keys via BYOK in some regions. Audit logs are available enterprise tier. We'll share the security pack.
[03:38] Elena Ramos: Who do we loop in for legal — are there standard MSAs or partner terms?
[03:45] Samir Patel: We'll share a partner MSA sketch and a draft SOW for pilots. Legal typically asks for co-term options — we can support a 12 month pilot term and convert to annual later.
[04:02] Maya Singh: Great. On accounts: we have three prioritized targets — Account A (large retail), Account B (regional bank), Account C (logistics). We want to table details now and align owners.
[04:18] Alex Chen: Let's map them. Account A — who is lead?
[04:22] Maya Singh: Elena will lead for Account A. Account B — Jon is the technical sponsor; Diego connects on infra. Account C — I'll own the business relationship.
[04:35] Alex Chen: Perfect. We propose a two-week quick pilot for Account A on Redwood Dedicated to validate latency under their expected seq lengths, then pilot B and C with measurement windows.
[04:48] Diego Morales: Two weeks might be short if Private deployment is needed. Can the Dedicated environment simulate their on-prem profile?
[05:00] Priya Nair: Dedicated can approximate hardware and provide identical kernel paths — but if they need an on-prem air-gapped build we can do that too, timeline is longer (4–6 weeks). For validation where latency is primary, Dedicated should be sufficient.
[05:20] Jon Park: What's the typical time to spin up a Dedicated pool?
[05:24] Alex Chen: Provisioning usually 3–5 business days after contract, assuming capacity available. If it's a new region we may need add'l lead time.
[05:36] Elena Ramos: Pricing — we need ranges to model expected commission. Could you give ballpark numbers?
[05:42] Alex Chen: I'll send official bands, but ballpark: for Dedicated starts at $Xk/month for a small pool, tiered down with utilization and commitments. For Hosted it's per-token. We'll email a pricing sheet.
[05:58] Maya Singh: Also curious about lead routing — if Greenlight sources a lead, how does the funnel kickoff happen in CRM? We have strict lead ownership rules.
[06:12] Samir Patel: We can implement an automated lead handoff in Salesforce with status tags (Partner-sourced, Partner-influenced). We prefer to create joint opportunity records with shared ownership fields.
[06:28] Diego Morales: Any integration work required with our CRM?
[06:33] Samir Patel: Minimal — mostly connectors and field mapping, we can provide the mapping doc.
[06:38] [crosstalk] Elena Ramos: Okay — and what about competitive positioning? We compete a bit with CloudSphere on price and with ForgeServe on on-prem capabilities. How do you position Redwood?
[06:52] Priya Nair: We lead on throughput and configurable routing — our differentiator is predictable inference economics plus multi-deploy modes. For regulated workloads we emphasize private deployment and auditability. We'll share a competitive battlecard.
[07:08] Alex Chen: Also worth noting our caching and batching wins can reduce token cost materially for LLM-heavy workflows which often matters in retail and logistics.
[07:20] Maya Singh: Sounds good. For pilot success criteria, let's list concrete pass/fail rules so legal and procurement can sign off.
[07:30] Alex Chen: Proposed criteria: p95 latency under X ms for the canonical prompt set, end-to-end cost delta less than Y% vs their current infra, and no functional regressions on a 200-sample evaluation. If these hit, we move to a joint proposal.
[07:48] Diego Morales: We also need a security checklist pass — SOC2/ISO certification evidence or compensating controls.
[07:56] Priya Nair: We'll attach SOC2 report and can walk through the controls. For Greenlight's needs we can outline compensating controls for any gaps.
[08:10] Elena Ramos: On go-to-market — what co-marketing assets can we expect? Joint press? Case study?
[08:17] Samir Patel: Standard co-marketing package includes a joint press release template, co-branded datasheet, and a joint webinar. Case studies typically after a successful pilot.
[08:29] Maya Singh: Good. I want to flag internal enablement — our SDRs need a one-pager to brief them on value props and talk tracks.
[08:38] Alex Chen: We'll send an SDR one-pager and a 20-minute enablement deck.
[08:45] Jon Park: Back to technical: how do you handle KV cache and context limits? We have large multi-turn dialogues, and caching behaviour will impact perf.
[08:58] Priya Nair: We support KV cache residency and eviction policies; for long multi-turn sessions we recommend streaming and incremental KV flush depending on recency. We'll share best-practices doc.
[09:12] Diego Morales: Any known model regressions when quantizing? We prefer 4-bit quant for cost but worried about hallucination risk.
[09:22] Priya Nain: (laughs) small typo — Priya Nair here — quantization is workload dependent. We provide quantization profiles and recommendation from Optimize. There's a tradeoff; we'll include quality regression thresholds in the test plan.
[09:40] Elena Ramos: Timeline — we want a pilot start within 3 weeks. Is that aggressive?
[09:46] Alex Chen: For Dedicated pilot yes, 3 weeks is doable assuming contracts and greenlight security questionnaire come back fast. For Private, longer.
[09:56] Maya Singh: We'll prioritize Account A for the fast path.
[10:00] [15:00 mark summary jump]
[15:02] Alex Chen: Quick recap of decisions so far: Account owners confirmed, pilot on Dedicated for Account A, need benchmark template completion, and security questionnaire.
[15:20] Maya Singh: Adding: Greenlight needs a joint exec brief after pilot; we want an internal signoff chat.
[15:31] Alex Chen: Noted.
[15:35] [22:00 mark]
[22:05] Elena Ramos: Procurement — can Redwood accept PO and standard commercial terms? We usually push for net-60.
[22:15] Samir Patel: We typically do net-30 but can be flexible for enterprise. For pilots we often request upfront or milestone billing.
[22:25] Maya Singh: We'll engage procurement early.
[22:28] Alex Chen: I'll loop in finance to propose options.
[22:33] [32:00 mark technical interlude]
[32:05] Priya Nair: Quick tech note: if Account A expects 200 token prompts at p95 under 400ms, we'll need to tune batch sizes and maybe a higher-tier GPU to hit that. We'll propose a config in the pilot plan.
[32:20] Diego Morales: Can you provide expected cost per 1k tokens estimates across configs?
[32:27] Priya Nair: Yes, we'll include a cost matrix comparing Hosted, Dedicated and quant modes.
[32:35] [40:00 mark commercial]
[40:05] Alex Chen: On partner comp — suggested approach: 60/40 for Greenlight-sourced, with accelerator credits for first 6 months. Also referral fee for influenced leads.
[40:20] Maya Singh: We'll need a written doc; our finance team needs to model quotas/commission.
[40:25] Samir Patel: We'll draft and attach.
[40:30] [50:00 mark risk discussion]
[50:05] Jon Park: Risk: if latency doesn't meet expectations, what's fallback? Can we burst to another region or fall back to a smaller model?
[50:15] Priya Nair: Yes, Redwood has routing policies and automatic fallback to compatible model variants. We'll configure canary routes and fallback thresholds. We'll provide a playbook.
[50:30] Diego Morales: Good — please include monitoring hooks and traces we can pull into our observability stack.
[50:36] Priya Nair: We'll include tracing hooks and a sample Grafana dashboard.
[50:44] [57:00 wrap-up]
[57:05] Alex Chen: Final recap and owners: Alex to send pricing & partner one-pager, Priya to send benchmark/test harness, Samir to send partner MSA sketch, Diego/Maya to deliver contact and security questionnaire. We'll target pilot kickoff Mar 10 (tentative).
[57:25] Maya Singh: Sounds good, appreciate the clarity.
[57:30] Elena Ramos: Thanks everyone.
[57:33] Alex Chen: Thanks — we'll follow up with the packet and calendar invites.
[57:40] [end of recording — informal chatter continues for a bit]
